findings.text: Ask 4 ("give the merge command and the restart steps") is not met: no file in the task folder tells the owner or a fresh agent how to land it. owner-step.md and task.jsonl say only "Branch worktree/remote-site-tunnel awaits merge", and the live gateway is running from the worktree (task.jsonl line 1). Add a hand-off line with the merge command (`node Servex/merge.mjs` or equivalent for `worktree/remote-site-tunnel`), then `node Server/Tunnel.mjs down && up` from the main tree so the gateway stops running from the worktree, and a note not to restart during a voice call.

Server/Tunnel.mjs:46 (diff line 287): `await new SiteGateway().listen()` runs inside the MCP tunnel's `up`, and the SiteGateway constructor throws when `SiteGateway.target()` finds no private LAN address (SiteGateway.mjs:54, which happens when the PC is offline or between networks) or when `remote.token` cannot be read. In either case the voice agent's MCP tunnel never starts. Wrap that call in try/catch so a site-gateway failure only logs, as the comment "a busy port only logs" already promises.

SiteGateway.mjs:53 has a typo in the 172.x part of the private-range regex: it reads `2d`, where `2\d` was meant, and the dots are unescaped. So 172.20–29 addresses are never matched. Use `WorktreePreview.lan_ip()` (Server/WorktreePreview.mjs:28), which already does this job, instead of a second copy (law 6, one of everything).

SiteGateway.mjs: the LAN address is read once, when the gateway starts. If DHCP gives the PC a new address, every request answers 502 "site unreachable" until `Tunnel.mjs` restarts. Re-reading the address after a connection error would fix it cheaply.

SiteGateway.mjs:105 takes any `?key=` query parameter as the login key. A page that uses its own `key` parameter would get the Locked page instead (a wrong key answers 401). Renaming the parameter to `site_key` would avoid the clash.

SiteGateway.mjs:39: DENY ends each route with `(\/|$)`, so a variant like `/mcp;x` passes the gateway. The dev server's own LAN guard still refuses it, because the gateway dials the LAN address. That makes this defence in depth only, but `(\/|$|[;.?])` or a plain prefix test would close it.

Server/README.md does not mention SiteGateway.mjs (nor Tunnel.mjs). Both are indexed only from Servex/ext/remote/doc/tunnel.md. A one-line entry under Server would let a reader find the public gateway from the Server index.

public/framework/dev/servex_url.js:12: the header comment still lists only three callers. This change adds DevBar/chat.js, ai/v/3/Prompts.js and core/Page/ai/live.js, and it adds `DEV_SITE`, which the readme does not name. Also, `DEV_SITE` begins `^(localhost|…` with no end anchor, so `localhost.anything` matches it. That is harmless (it only decides whether Servex is probed).
chat.js no longer reads the `window.__SERVEX_URL__` override. grep finds no code that sets it, so nothing breaks.
The links in network-map.md to `Servex/...` and `Server/...` resolve in the repo but not on the site, because only `public/` is served.
